messages.content: I need to put together a quick Atlanta trip for a donor reception and two site meetings. The reception is Tuesday at 6:00 p.m. in Midtown. On Wednesday I have a 9:00 to 11:00 meeting near the West End station and a 1:00 to 3:30 meeting back in Midtown. I can leave Dallas Tuesday morning and come home Wednesday after the last meeting. Please build the flights, one hotel night, and ground transportation.
What dates are Tuesday and Wednesday, and should I compare both Love Field and DFW? Also, will you check a bag, or can I plan around carry-on travel?

September 16 and 17. Compare both airports. Carry-on only, and no rental car. I can use MARTA and hired rides, but I do not want a plan that depends on everything going perfectly before the reception.

I found two useful outbound patterns. From Love Field, a nonstop leaving at 8:10 a.m. reaches Atlanta at 11:15 a.m. local time. From DFW, a nonstop leaving at 7:35 a.m. arrives at 10:45 a.m. Both leave more than six hours before the reception. There is also a cheaper DFW departure arriving at 2:55 p.m., but I would drop it: one meaningful delay would put the reception at risk. Are you able to leave Midtown promptly when the Wednesday meeting ends at 3:30?
Yes. The meeting organizer says it will end at 3:30, and the venue is about a five-minute walk from the Midtown MARTA station. I would need to collect my bag from the hotel first.

That makes a 6:35 p.m. Atlanta departure workable if the hotel is near the station and will hold your bag. Allow about 15 minutes to walk from the meeting, retrieve it, and reach the platform, then roughly 30 minutes on MARTA. That should put you at the airport around 4:20 to 4:35, about two hours before departure. A 5:25 flight is technically possible but does not provide a dependable margin, so I am excluding it.
Good. What are the actual flight combinations and prices?

The Love Field combination is the Tuesday 8:10 a.m. nonstop to Atlanta, arriving 11:15 a.m., with the Wednesday 6:35 p.m. nonstop back, arriving at Love Field at 7:55 p.m. The current round-trip fare is $278. The DFW combination leaves Tuesday at 7:35 a.m., arrives at 10:45 a.m., and returns Wednesday at 7:10 p.m., reaching DFW at 8:35 p.m.; it is $226. Both fares include a carry-on in the displayed terms, but the live checkout page still needs to confirm that.
The DFW return gives me more time, but getting home that late is not ideal. Show me Midtown hotels that make the Wednesday departure easy.

The strongest fit is the Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta Midtown, about a three-minute walk from Arts Center station. A refundable king room is showing at $219 before tax and $255.67 mandatory total for one night. Breakfast and Wednesday luggage storage are listed, but storage should be confirmed directly because it matters to the return plan. The Hyatt Centric Midtown is about a six-minute walk from Midtown station at $229 before tax and approximately $267.70 total. Its listing also indicates luggage storage, though the payment page needs to confirm there is no added destination charge.
Which is better for the two meetings? The reception is near Colony Square, and the Wednesday afternoon site is two blocks south of the Arts Center station.

The Hampton is better for the full schedule. It is close to the afternoon site and Arts Center station, so you can retrieve your bag without doubling back. On Tuesday, MARTA from the airport to Arts Center takes about 25 to 30 minutes, and Colony Square is roughly a 15-minute walk or a short ride from the hotel. On Wednesday morning, a hired ride to the West End site is more direct than taking rail and walking with morning traffic around the station.
Estimate transportation both ways, including getting to the Dallas airport. Use rides from home in Dallas rather than parking.

For Love Field, budget $36 each way from home, or $72 total. For DFW, use $48 each way, or $96 total. In Atlanta, I would use MARTA from the airport to Arts Center for $2.50, allow $20 for a Wednesday morning ride to the West End site, $18 from West End back to Midtown, and use MARTA from Arts Center to the airport for another $2.50. That is $43 in Atlanta after allowing a small cushion above the likely ride quotes.
Would walking from the West End station to the morning site save enough to matter?

Not much. Rail would cost only $2.50, but the site is about a 14-minute walk from the station and you would need a transfer from Arts Center. It adds handling time before a fixed 9:00 meeting to save roughly $17. The hired ride is the more dependable choice that morning. Rail remains the better airport option because it avoids interstate traffic and both the hotel and final site are close to stations.
Give me complete totals for the Hampton with each flight option. Do not include meals because those will be handled separately.

With Love Field, the estimate is $648.67: $278 airfare, $255.67 hotel, $72 Dallas airport rides, and $43 Atlanta transportation. With DFW, it is $620.67: $226 airfare, $255.67 hotel, $96 Dallas airport rides, and $43 in Atlanta. The DFW plan saves $28 overall, leaves Atlanta 35 minutes later, and gets back to the Dallas area 40 minutes later.
The difference is small enough that I would rather use Love Field and be home earlier. Is there any reason to take a hired ride from Atlanta airport to the hotel Tuesday instead of the train?

Only if the train has a service disruption or you land with less than about two hours before you need to be at the reception. On the planned arrival, MARTA should get you to Arts Center around noon, leaving nearly six hours. Even allowing time for lunch, hotel check-in, and a short delay, the margin is substantial. A hired ride could cost $35 to $50 and may take longer in afternoon traffic, so it is best retained as a contingency rather than included in the base plan.
Check the Wednesday sequence closely. I do not want to discover that the hotel will not give me the bag quickly enough or that the train timing is too tight.

The sequence is sound if two items are verified. Leave the West End meeting at 11:00 and take the planned ride to Midtown, which should put you near the afternoon site well before 1:00. Before that meeting, your bag remains with the Hampton. At 3:30, walk two blocks to the hotel, retrieve it, and continue to Arts Center station. Set 3:55 as the target for entering the station and 4:10 as the latest comfortable train. Typical travel time to the airport is about 30 minutes, leaving roughly two hours before the 6:35 flight. If the meeting runs beyond 3:45 or MARTA reports disruption, switch to a hired ride immediately.
Keep one backup return in case the 6:35 fare changes. I do not need a whole new itinerary, just something that still works after the meeting.

Retain the 7:10 p.m. Atlanta-to-DFW nonstop as the backup. It is currently available within the $226 DFW round trip and gives another 35 minutes at departure, although it means using DFW for both directions and arriving there at 8:35 p.m. A later Love Field nonstop is not pricing competitively in the current results. Do not mix the outbound and return airports unless the separate one-way totals and Dallas ground transportation are recalculated.
Summarize the decision, the reimbursable amount, and exactly what still has to be checked. Do not book anything yet.

Use the Love Field plan as the lead option: Tuesday's 8:10 a.m. nonstop to Atlanta, arriving at 11:15 a.m.; one refundable night at the Hampton Inn & Suites Atlanta Midtown; and Wednesday's 6:35 p.m. nonstop back to Love Field, arriving at 7:55 p.m. Use MARTA for both airport transfers, hired rides between Midtown and the West End site, and rides between home and Love Field. The current reimbursable estimate is $648.67, excluding meals. Before purchase, verify the $278 airfare, nonstop times, carry-on allowance, and change or cancellation terms; confirm the hotel's $255.67 mandatory total, refundable deadline, and complimentary luggage storage through at least 4:00 p.m. Wednesday; and check MARTA service notices for both travel windows. Keep the 7:10 p.m. DFW return combination as the backup if the Love Field fare or schedule changes. Nothing has been booked.
